issues.description: The template header declares the class as 'Image24' while the implementation file and the rest of the code use 'Bitmap24' (constructors and methods are named Bitmap24). This name mismatch between declaration and definition will cause compilation failures and confuses students about the intended class name and API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' and ensure constructor and method declarations use 'Bitmap24' so the header matches the implementation. Alternatively, rename the implementation to match the header, but updating the header to 'Bitmap24' preserves the intended API used throughout the codebase.

issues.description: The template header file declares the class as 'Image24' (in Bitmap24.hpp) while the implementation file and filenames use 'Bitmap24'. The solution repository uses 'Bitmap24' consistently. This mismatch between the header declaration and the implementation name creates a direct mapping and compilation confusion for students (they will search for Bitmap24 in the header but find Image24) and increases extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' so the header, implementation, and filenames are consistent (e.g., change 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' and adjust include guards or any references accordingly). This aligns the template with the solution's naming and removes the misleading discrepancy.
